# How to Use This Field Manual {.unnumbered}

This work is structured as an **Architectural Field Manual and Systems Blueprint**. It is designed to guide you through assembling, measuring, and qualifying a complete physical AI machine from scratch.

---

## The Anatomy of a Physical AI Agent

Rather than teaching disconnected algorithms, every chapter in this manual installs and validates one vital organ of the agent:

| Part and Focus | Chapters and Systems Organs | Core Systems Mechanism |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Part I: The Physical Foundation** | • Ch 1: Physical Causality<br>• Ch 2: Time and Latency<br>• Ch 3: Multi-Rate Systems | • Matter, momentum, and irreversibility<br>• Freshness decay ($\Delta t$) and $P_{99}$ latency tails<br>• Lock-free IPC and MCU watchdog crash survival |
| **Part II: The Agent Architecture** | • Ch 4: Perception<br>• Ch 5: Memory<br>• Ch 6: Reasoning<br>• Ch 7: Planning<br>• Ch 8: Reflex | • Photons to DMA taxes and ViT spatial tokens<br>• Temporal belief buffers and latent world models (JEPAs)<br>• 1 Hz VLM expiring intent leases ($t_{\text{expire}}$)<br>• 20–50 Hz action chunking (Diffusion/ACT) and $\mathcal{C}^2$ ensembling<br>• 1 kHz MCU safety vetoes and stopping bounds ($d_{\text{stop}}$) |
| **Part III: Integration and Release** | • Ch 9: Placement<br>• Ch 10: Governance<br>• Ch 11: Release | • Whole-system resource ledgers (FLOPs/SRAM/Watts)<br>• Bumpless joystick overrides and truncated logs<br>• STPA hazards, HIL ladders, and the CAE safety case |
| **Capstone: Final System Defense** | • Ch 12: Capstone | • Seeded hardware/software fault recovery and release sign-off |

---

## The Cumulative Design Dossier

In traditional engineering courses, students write a free-form final report after the project is already finished.

In this manual, you build an accumulating, versioned **Cumulative Design Dossier** that evolves chapter-by-chapter. Every chapter freezes a specific, checkable engineering artifact:

| Chapter | Capability Installed | Dossier Artifact Produced |
| :---: | :--- | :--- |
| **1** | System Boundary and Causal Scope | `Loop Charter` (`LOOP-01`) |
| **2** | Dynamic Deadlines and Latency Budgets | `Requirements and Assumptions Ledger` (`REQ-01`) |
| **3** | Multi-Rate Scheduling and Fault Isolation | `Continuous Runtime Skeleton` (`RUN-01`) |
| **4** | Sensory Acquisition and Bus Priorities | `Observation Contract` (`OBS-01`) |
| **5** | Spatial State and Uncertainty Horizons | `State, Frames and Timing Model` (`STATE-01`) |
| **6** | Semantic Goal Grounding and Intent | `Policy Interface and Intent Schema` (`INTENT-01`) |
| **7** | Continuous Trajectory Rollouts | `Planning and Trajectory Schema` (`PLAN-01`) |
| **8** | Real-Time Physical Limits and Vetoes | `Action Limits and Enforcement Design` (`ENF-01`) |
| **9** | Silicon Resource Allocation | `Placement Map and Resource Ledger` (`PLACE-01`) |
| **10** | Human Overrides and Provenance Logging | `Human-Authority and Governed Data Record` (`AUTH-01`) |
| **11** | ODD Qualification and CAE Safety Case | `Integrated Deployment Case` (`REL-01`) |

At the end of the journey, your completed dossier forms the empirical basis for rendering a formal **Deploy**, **Condition** (deploy with restricted operating bounds), or **Refuse** release verdict.

---

## The Three Ways to Use This Material

1. **For University Cohorts (e.g., ETH Zurich Project Seminar):**
   * Follow the 14-week schedule in `course/syllabus.md`.
   * Complete the core physical hardware milestones on the TinyAgents Kit.
   * Present at the Midterm Design Review (T3) and defend your final dossier under instructor-seeded faults at the Final Defense (T5).
2. **For Self-Learners and Kit Builders:**
   * Work through Chapters 1 to 11 at your own pace with the Arduino UNO Q on your desk.
   * Use the tested starter checkpoints in `labs/` so a bug in one section never blocks you from progressing.
3. **For Practicing Engineers:**
   * Use the individual chapters as modular systems contracts for architecting real-world autonomous systems, quadrotors, rovers, or robotic manipulators.
